criteria.descriptor: Correctly diagnoses the resample-before-split leakage, why ROC-AUC misleads under extreme imbalance (huge TN base keeps FPR low), and the base-rate/calibration distortion from 50/50 rebalancing, with an accurate fix (prior correction or recalibration on true-prior data). No incorrect claims (e.g. that 'balancing fixes' the threshold, or that ROC-AUC is fine here). Full marks require accurate mechanisms, not just naming the right buzzwords.

Covers all four asked dimensions — flawed steps, replacement metrics, imbalance handling, and probability/threshold-under-budget validation — and ties the metric and threshold explicitly to the ~200-review/day constraint. Loses points for skipping calibration/prior-correction, the budget-linked operating point, or the evaluation-on-true-prior/temporal-split point.

Justifies each recommendation with the underlying mechanism (why leakage inflates the score, why FPR stays low, why 50/50 over-predicts, why a budget makes it a ranking problem) rather than asserting best-practice labels. Credit for weighing SMOTE vs class weights vs threshold-tuning rather than reflexively picking one.

Organised as a clear critique-then-redesign that a review audience could act on, using correct vocabulary (leakage, PR-AUC/average precision, precision/recall@budget, calibration, prior shift, scale_pos_weight, out-of-time split) precisely and concisely.

expected_answer_points: Applying SMOTE (or any resampling) before the train/test split leaks synthetic points across the split and inflates the reported metric; resampling must be confined to the training partition / inside each CV fold, with validation and test kept at the true prior.

ROC-AUC is misleading under 0.2% prevalence because the vast negative count keeps FPR low despite many false positives; report PR-AUC / average precision and budget-tied operating points (precision@~200/day and recall at that alert volume) instead.

Rebalancing to 50/50 shifts the base rate the model learns, so predicted probabilities are inflated/miscalibrated versus the true prior and must be prior-corrected in log-odds space or recalibrated (Platt/isotonic) on true-distribution data.

The fixed 0.5 threshold is invalid after rebalancing/calibration; the operating threshold (or top-k) must be tuned on a true-prior validation set to fill the ~200 review/day budget while maximising recall — a ranking-under-budget framing.

Consider cost-sensitive learning / class weights (e.g. XGBoost scale_pos_weight) as an alternative to SMOTE, and benchmark against threshold-tuning alone, noting SMOTE pitfalls (no new signal, poor behaviour with categorical/high-dimensional features, noisy borderline synthetics).

Evaluate on an untouched test set with the real prior, and for fraud specifically prefer a temporal / out-of-time split over a random split to avoid future-information leakage and reflect concept drift.
Address production validation/monitoring: track calibration and precision/recall at the review budget over time, accounting for delayed/uncertain fraud labels.
common_pitfalls: Focuses only on 'SMOTE vs undersampling' and misses that the primary error is resampling before the split, which is what actually inflates the 0.97.

Accepts ROC-AUC (or proposes accuracy/F1 at 0.5) as the reporting metric, failing to explain why FPR-based metrics look great at 0.2% prevalence, and never connects the metric to the 200-alert/day budget.

Treats the 0.5 threshold as fine 'because the data is now balanced', ignoring that rebalancing inflates predicted probabilities and that calibration / prior correction is required before any threshold is meaningful.
Tries to fix bad production precision with more aggressive resampling instead of threshold-tuning / top-k ranking against the fixed review capacity.
Uses a random split for fraud data, overlooking temporal leakage and concept drift that an out-of-time split guards against.
Gives generic advice ('get more data', 'try deep learning', 'use class weights') without engaging the budget-constrained operating point or the calibration consequence of resampling.
reference_answer:
The methodology is broken in three compounding ways, and the headline 0.97 is not trustworthy.

1) SMOTE before the split is data leakage. SMOTE interpolates each synthetic minority point between a real minority sample and its nearest minority neighbours. Doing this on the full dataset means synthetic points in the test set are built from training points (and vice-versa), so the test set is contaminated. Resampling must happen only on the training partition, and inside each CV fold — the validation/test sets must keep the true 0.2% prior. Fix this first: split (ideally an out-of-time / temporal split, since fraud patterns drift and a random split leaks future behaviour), then resample only the training side.

2) ROC-AUC is the wrong headline metric here. With 99.8% negatives, the FPR denominator is enormous, so thousands of false positives barely move FPR — ROC-AUC can sit at 0.97 while precision at any reviewable alert volume is terrible. Report PR-AUC / average precision, and, decisively, operating-point metrics tied to the budget: recall (frauds caught) when the alert volume is capped at ~200/day (~0.4% of 50k), i.e. precision@200 and recall@200. This is really a ranking-under-budget problem: rank transactions by score and see how many true frauds fall in the top ~200.

3) Rebalancing to 50/50 destroys probability calibration and makes 0.5 meaningless. The model now learns P(fraud|x) under a 50/50 prior and massively over-predicts fraud relative to the real 0.2% base rate, which is exactly why production alerts explode. Either prior-correct the scores in log-odds space (subtract the training prior log-odds, add the true prior log-odds) or recalibrate (Platt/isotonic) on a held-out set that has the true distribution. Then do NOT use 0.5: tune the threshold (or take top-k) on a true-prior validation set to fill the ~200/day budget while maximising recall.

Corrected pipeline: temporal split → within training folds, handle imbalance via cost-sensitive weighting (XGBoost scale_pos_weight) or modest resampling, and benchmark it against doing nothing but threshold-tuning, since SMOTE adds no real signal and misbehaves with categorical/high-cardinality features. Evaluate on the untouched, true-prior (and out-of-time) test set using PR-AUC and precision/recall at the 200-alert budget. Calibrate, pick the operating threshold to hit the budget, and in production monitor calibration and precision@budget over time (accounting for delayed fraud labels).
